To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the EM failure time of a Cu column bump can be extended by 3-5X when the diameter is increased by 1.5X and the bump height is increased by 2.5X, and that the bump height is more important than the bump diameter in determining the EM lifetime of a Cu column.
the EM failure time of the BOL/bump increases with decreasing bump size, increasing bump height and decreasing bump pad width.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: (i) EM behavior of copper column bumps under different temperature and current density; (ii) EM failure mechanisms of the bumps; (iii) EM design rules for copper bumps.

the following objectives: 1) to develop a comprehensive understanding of the EM failure mechanisms in Cu bumps; 2) to develop a robust design rule for BOL/bump to ensure the reliability of high current/high temperature conditions; 3) to develop a new EM model for Cu bumps; and 4) to develop a design of experiment (DoE) for Cu bumps.
understanding the effect of temperature and current on the electromigration of Cu column bump and establishing the robust design rules for BOL/bump.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current density and temperature of Cu bump are the two main parameters that influence the EM lifetime.
a BOL/bump size of 20 um or larger with a current density of less than 1.5E5 A/cm2 is required to meet 1000 hours MTTF.
the EM reliability of Cu column bumps is strongly affected by temperature and current density.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the EM reliability of Cu column bumps can be improved by optimizing the bump geometry, such as reducing the bump size, increasing the bump height, and increasing the bump pad width, and by optimizing the solder composition.
the EM lifetime of Cu column bumps is very sensitive to the current density, temperature, bump size, bump pitch, bump pad size and bump height.
the EM failure mechanism in Cu column bump has been identified as a combination of electromigration and thermomigration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EM is a serious reliability challenge for Cu column BOL and bump.
the EM lifetime of Cu column bump is strongly dependent on the temperature/current conditions.
the current density and bump temperature have a major impact on the reliability of Cu column bumps.
